newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Alcatel to announce Skybridge partners.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel to announce Skybridge partners.

text.p: French telecoms equipment group Alcatel Alsthom expects to announce partners for its Skybridge telecommunications satellite project by the end of June, said a company official on Wednesday.
Herve Sorre, Skybridge marketing director at Alcatel Espace told Reuters ahead of a news briefing the project was likely to raise an initial capital of US$150 million through equity offering in 1997.
He said among the various ways of raising capital for the US$3.5 billion project was a possible initial public offering.
"We will raise an initial capital of US$150 million in 1997 and more in 1998 when we enter into signigicant contracts with manufacturers," Sorre said.
He added that financing through an equity issue was likely to make up 30 percent of the project cost.

Partners for the Skybridge satellite project, which is intended to provide high capacity Internet access as well as other applications like teleworking, distance learning and mobile communications, were expected to come from the U.S., Asia and Europe.
Sorre said Skybridge had been speaking to U.S. satellite maker Loral Space & Communications Ltd but declined to give details on other potential partners.
Alcatel was likely to take up 50 percent of the initial US$150 million equity in Skybridge.
On the possibility of listing Skybridge, Sorre said it was likely to be on the New York Stock Exchange.

"It depends on the condition of the market and how the market reacts to other projects like Globalstar Telecommunications Ltd and Iridium World Communications Ltd. They will influence the condition of the market," Sorre said.
The Skybridge project will have eight spare satellites on top of the 64 core satellites. Sorre said 32 satellites will be launch in the first phase in 2001.
